findings.summary: Duplicate invalid tags possible when same invalid tag appears in both body and subject
findings.detail: The code does `all_invalid_tags = body_invalid_tags + subject_invalid_tags`. If the same invalid tag (e.g., `{{Typo}}`) appears in both body and subject, it will appear twice in the `all_invalid_tags` array. The original code did not deduplicate either (Mustache::Template.tags can return the same tag name once per occurrence, and a single template could theoretically have duplicates), so this is consistent with existing behavior. The `has_invalid_tags` boolean is unaffected. Impact is cosmetic at most -- if the frontend ever displays the invalid tags list, duplicates would show.
findings.spec_requirement: Widen invalid_tags computation to include subject template tags
findings.assessment: Consistent with existing behavior. No functional impact. Not a bug -- just noting the behavior.

findings.summary: Invalid CSS: font-size property doubled via t.text.sm theme utility
findings.detail: Line `font-size: ${t.text.sm};` produces invalid CSS because `t.text.sm` is already a complete CSS declaration that includes `font-size:`. The output becomes `font-size: font-size: 0.875rem;`. This is the exact pattern documented in the pipeline CLAUDE.md Known Failure Pattern #1 (which was motivated by this very feature's prior review round). The correct usage is `${t.text.sm};` as a standalone statement. NOTE: This file is outside my assigned focus area (my assigned files are job_application.rb and candidates_controller.rb), but it directly consumes render_template_message output, so I am flagging it. It may be flagged by the reviewer assigned to frontend files.
